summary: Ngari Gunsa Airport (NGQ/ZUAL) is a high-altitude airport serving Shiquanhe, the administrative seat of Ali Prefecture in far western Tibet, China. Sitting at roughly 4,274 meters (14,022 feet) above sea level, it is among the highest commercial airports in the world and the primary air gateway to the sacred Mount Kailash pilgrimage circuit. The airport handles a limited schedule of domestic flights, primarily connecting the remote region to Lhasa and other major Chinese cities.
faqs:
Q: What is the elevation of Ngari Gunsa Airport?
A: The airport sits at approximately 4,274 meters (14,022 feet) above sea level, making it one of the highest commercial airports in the world.

Q: Which cities have direct flights to Ngari Gunsa?
A: Direct flights primarily connect to Lhasa, with additional seasonal or limited service to Chengdu, Kashgar, and other Chinese cities operated by Tibet Airlines and other carriers.

Q: Can tourists visit Mount Kailash from this airport?
A: Yes, the airport is the main entry point for travelers undertaking the Mount Kailash kora (pilgrimage circuit), though overland travel from the airport to the mountain still takes many hours.

Q: What is the best season to fly into Ngari Gunsa?
A: The warm and dry months from May to October are recommended, as winter conditions and extreme cold can disrupt flights and make overland travel difficult.
transport_tips: The airport is located about 3-5 kilometers from Shiquanhe town, typically reached by taxi or pre-arranged hotel pickup in a short 10-15 minute drive. Flight schedules are infrequent and weather-related delays or cancellations are common, so build buffer days into any travel itinerary. Public transport options are limited; arranging private transport or joining a tour group with airport transfer is advisable for most visitors.
local_tip: Due to the extreme altitude, spend at least 24-48 hours acclimatizing in Shiquanhe before attempting the strenuous drive to Mount Kailash, and consider booking your return flight with a full spare day in case of weather-related cancellations, which are frequent at this elevation.
